subject: Quantica dedicated footprint intake — workload details requested
messages:
From: Emilia Santos <emilia@quantica.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quantica workload snapshot and questions

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Per our call, attached is a 48-hour sample trace (quantica_workload_profile.csv) and a tiny set of latency samples (latency_samples.json). High-level details below so you can start sizing:

- Primary workload: multi-tenant chat assistant (single-turn + short multi-turn sessions) integrated into our support product.
- Average QPS: 12 sustained, typical daytime window 08:00–20:00 PT.
- Peak QPS (observed within sample): 185 sustained for ~20 minutes; we expect spikes up to ~250 during marketing events.
- Concurrency estimate (active requests waiting on inference): baseline ~30, peak concurrent requests ~180.
- Prompt length (tokens): median 90, 75th pct 160, 95th pct 420.
- Response length (tokens): median 320, 75th pct 520, 95th pct 1,100.
- Percent of requests that require <300ms P95: ~40% (low-latency paths), remainder OK with up to 1s P95.
- Model preference: happy to test Redwood-optimized Llama-class quantized models; we prefer an int8/4 quantized variant if quality holds.
- Caching: some prefix reuse possible for templated prompts (~18% prefix reuse), full KV caching is unlikely across sessions because prompts include session-specific context.
- Other: ~6% of calls also call an embeddings endpoint (separate service), and ~3% need function/tool calling that triggers small I/O.

Security/compliance: we can sign an NDA and share heavier traces if needed; SOC2 proof will be required for Dedicated.

Attached files: quantica_workload_profile.csv (48h sample), latency_samples.json (p95/p99 micro-traces).

Would love your take on an initial GPU footprint (ballpark) and whether batching or caching knobs could materially change node counts.

Best,
Emilia Santos
Head of ML Ops
Quantica.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emilia Santos <emilia@quantica.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantica workload snapshot and questions

Emilia —

Received, thanks for the attachments and the clear numbers. This is great. We’ll put together a short pre-sales sizing note and a couple of footprint options (latency-optimized vs cost-optimized) for QUANT-2026-087.

A few quick clarifying items that will materially affect sizing if you can confirm:
- Are the 95th-percentile response sizes (up to ~1,100 tokens) generated by the model, or are you truncating longer responses client-side?
- Are there predictable scheduled spikes (e.g., marketing campaigns) with forecasted QPS >250? If so, how long do those spikes last?
- Do you expect per-request function/tool calls to be synchronous on the critical path?
- Any restriction on model families / ability to accept aggressively quantized variants (int8/in4)?

If you prefer, I can also run a quick synthetic stress test with a small dedicated cluster and share observed P95s for an initial mapping.

I’ll loop in Ben and Dev for a preliminary node-count sketch and will aim to have a first-pass within 48 business hours.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-08-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantica workload snapshot and questions — pre-sales sizing request (QUANT-2026-087)

Ben / Dev —

Forwarding Quantica’s 48h sample and quick notes (below). Deal: QUANT-2026-087, region: us. Quantica is targeting a Dedicated deployment with an initial commit and needs a footprint estimate to include in procurement.

Key numbers from their sample: avg QPS 12, observed peak 185 (they expect spikes to ~250), peak concurrent requests ~180, median prompt 90 tokens, median response 320 tokens, 95th response ~1,100 tokens. They have ~18% prefix reuse and ~6% embedding calls. P95 latency target: ~300ms for ~40% of requests; others can tolerate up to 1s.

Please provide a short first-pass:
- Node count and GPU SKU (latency-optimized and cost-optimized variants)
- Assumptions on batching (max batch size), KV / prefix cache impact, and token throughput per GPU that you used for calc
- Any questions that would change the estimate (e.g., exact p95 target for 95th-percentile responses, tolerable qps during spikes)

Attachments: forwarded quantica_workload_profile.csv; latency_samples.json

Timing: they’ve asked for a vendor footprint to include in an RFP timeline — can we aim for a brief sketch by Friday (2026-08-21)?

Thanks —
Chloe

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quantica workload snapshot and questions — pre-sales sizing request (QUANT-2026-087)

Chloe / Dev —

Quick first-pass (ballpark) based on their numbers and our recent benchmarks:

Assumptions used:
- Model: Redwood-65B quantized int8 (good mix of perf/quality).
- Avg token generation per request = prompt (120 tokens assumed) + response (420 tokens assumed for sizing headroom).
- Effective tokens/s per A100-80GB (int8) with batching ~ 9k tokens/s; H100-80GB ~ 16k tokens/s (numbers vary with seq len).
- Target: serve P95 <= 300ms for their low-latency subset (40%) and P95 <= 1s for bulk. We map these to two service tiers (hot/cold) if they want strict guarantees.

Latency-optimized option:
- H100-80GB nodes x 8 (approx). Config: smaller batch sizes (<=32), aggressive kernel selection, dedicated hot pool to keep KV cache/warm keys. Estimated concurrent capacity: ~200–250 concurrent low-latency requests with headroom for bursts to 350 QPS.

Cost-optimized option:
- A100-80GB nodes x 10–12 (approx). Config: larger batching (<=128) for throughput, rely on prefix caching where possible (their 18% reuse reduces gross token load by ~12%). Expected to meet average throughput and 1s P95, but hot-path P95 for 40% of requests will be higher than their 300ms target unless we carve a small hot pool (2–3 H100 or A100-optimized nodes).

If they accept stronger quantization (in4) we can shave ~25–35% off node counts at some quality risk. Embeddings workload (6%) can be routed to a small shared CPU/GPU pool — negligible impact.

Follow-ups / open items:
- Need confirmation on the exact percent of requests that must hit 300ms P95 (is it 40% or 'top 40% of customers'?).
- Ask whether spikes to 250 QPS are predictable/scheduled (sustained 20+ minutes vs minute-long bursts significantly changes autoscaling needs).
- Do they want a mixed-instance (H100 hot, A100 cold) proposal? That fits the SLA profile and reduces cost.

I’ll draft a 1-page vendor footprint with the two options and the key assumptions for Chloe to send back to Quantica.

—Ben
Ben Carter
